newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FERC orders El Paso to serve Southwestern.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FERC orders El Paso to serve Southwestern.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission on Wednesday ordered El Paso Electric Co to transmit power from Southwestern Public Service Co to the municipal utility in Las Cruces, New Mexico.

El Paso, which up to now has provided power to customers in Las Cruces, rejected two transmission service requests by Southwestern, saying that the utility had failed to say when the service should start and how much capacity it would need.
Las Cruces, which set up a municipal utility, is trying to take over El Paso's distribution lines in the city and has agreed to buy bulk power from Southwestern instead of El Paso.
The commission said El Paso must now respond to Southwestern's request for transmission service in 30 days.

With the city utility planning to switch power suppliers, Las Cruces asked the FERC to decide whether it would eventually have to pay El Paso to cover the costs of generation facilities it built to serve the city.

The commission said Wednesday that the question should be addressed at a hearing, where El Paso would have to prove that it had little reason to believe Las Cruces would stop being a customer. If it did so, the utilities would then discuss how much El Paso should be allowed to collect from the city to cover its stranded costs.
